comparator.name: Computer Science
comparator.sourceNotes: The 2026–27 regulations, Appendix C, specify a 135 EC major and 45 EC profiling space. The major includes 75 EC of compulsory courses, six 7.5 EC restricted electives and a required 15 EC team Software Project. The generic example selects Imperatief programmeren and the first six listed electives. Algoritmiek and Data-analyse en retrieval contribute the required 15 EC of advanced electives. The separate profiling space includes at least 15 EC at levels 2–3 and excludes overlapping courses. The official 2026 teaching blocks allow the introductory project, databases and web technology in Year 1, followed by functional programming, software engineering, concurrency and the later electives. The published Year 3 plan allows research methods in period 1 before the project in periods 3–4. Project registration follows an invitation from the programme. An optional individual thesis can be taken in the profiling space alongside the required software project. Zero-credit compulsory tutorials are outside the credit total.

alternatives.label: Computer Systems, Software and Algorithms
alternatives.concept: Build software and study how computer systems handle data. Progress from programming and logic to networks, databases, software construction and advanced algorithms. Apply these foundations to machine learning, computer vision and intelligent agents.
alternatives.labelReason: Build software and study how computer systems handle data. Progress from programming and logic to networks, databases, software construction and advanced algorithms. Apply these foundations to machine learning, computer vision and intelligent agents.
progression: Six terms of four courses include Personal & Professional Development in Year 1 and 6 level-300 courses. Programming and logic precede the algorithms sequence, and linear algebra precedes advanced algorithms and later data and AI work.

candidates.label: Educational minor in computer-science teaching
candidates.assessment: The official educational minor includes subject didactics and supervised secondary-school teaching. Rhetoric and software study do not supply that teaching progression.

selection.assessment: One coherent option covers software, computing systems, algorithms, data and AI. Utrecht’s informal elective groupings support this shared plan. Its formal Game Technology direction was checked separately against UCR visual computing, interaction, AI and design. Those contributions provide partial coverage without a sustained game-design and game-development sequence. The educational minor requires subject didactics and a supervised school placement. No additional direction meets the programme-level standard.

notes.text: Utrecht requires separate courses in computer architecture, functional programming and concurrency, and a 15 EC team project. UCR covers parts of those subjects within broader systems and software courses. IT law and Web Technology are examples of Utrecht’s restricted electives.

audience.programmeDescription: Utrecht’s Computer Science bachelor studies how computer systems work and how to design and test software. This example shows the general Dutch-taught degree and its required team software project.
audience.comparisonExplanation: The UCR option combines programming, databases, operating systems, algorithms and mathematical foundations with data and AI. Utrecht also offers a 15 EC individual thesis within its profiling space, alongside the required team project.
